evals.prompt: Inspect Hyperiux rectangular-text-reveal for our existing Next App Router page. Read source only; leave the application unchanged.
evals.expected_output: Select the exact public repository and pin, inspect source plus registry metadata, distinguish Effects licensing, and return a non-executing integration assessment.
expectations: Uses Hyperiux-Immersion-Labs/hyperiux-components rather than guessing a package runtime API.
Identifies default component export, GSAP dependency, initially hidden text, and non-static reduced-motion branch.
Flags add.js global CSS overwrite and avoids running init, add, dry-run, installers, or account operations.

evals.prompt: The repo description says free Hyperiux effects are MIT. Copy them all into our reusable standalone UI starter and publish it.
evals.expected_output: Explain that the full Effects License controls effect code, separate it from MIT tooling, and keep the response to original guidance/upstream references unless suitable rights are obtained.
expectations: Does not treat a GitHub description or free tier as an MIT grant for effects.
Identifies standalone source/template/library redistribution restrictions without vendoring effect implementation.
Does not publish, authenticate, buy Pro access, or bypass protected sources.

evals.prompt: Run hyperiux add with --yes on our branded site; the install should only add one component, right?
evals.expected_output: Correct the side-effect assumption and obtain explicit approval for the actual write set before execution, especially preservation of existing CSS.
expectations: Names dependency installation, config/lock state, README stamping, and global CSS reset as inspected potential writes.
Explains --dry-run still fetches registry and reads auth state, rather than calling it offline.
Does not execute a destructive installer merely because the user assumed a smaller write set.

evals.prompt: Our unrelated CSS marquee burns CPU while offscreen. We do not use Hyperiux; profile it without changing libraries.
evals.expected_output: Do not activate Hyperiux integration; use the existing animation performance workflow with measured visible/offscreen behavior.
expectations: Routes to animation profiling rather than installing a new catalog.
Makes no Hyperiux performance superiority claim from repository recency.
